## You must change `src/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [src/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.

## The failure-assertion rule does not apply here

This phase declares `failure_assert: not_applicable`, so the gate does NOT
require a test asserting that a failure is produced. Your subsystem reports
problems as diagnostics or emits documents, so there is no `Result::Err` to

## Evidence — verified finding

```
src/stdlib.rs:7 declares `pub const MODULES: __FINDING__[__FINDING__str] = __FINDING__["bytes", "console", "csv", "files", "json", "list", "network", "sys", "time"]` and src/analyzer.rs rejects any other bare receiver as `Unknown variable`. SPEC.md's Standard Library section documents seven module headings that do not agree with it: `### text` (SPEC.md:950), `### math` (SPEC.md:959), `### formats` (SPEC.md:994) and `### console` (SPEC.md:942) — the last three of those names are absent from MODULES. Verified against the built binary, one call per documented module: `text.uppercase("hi")` fails with `AnalyzerError: Unknown variable 'text'`, `math.sqrt(9)` with `Unknown variable 'math'`, `formats.parse_json("{}")` with `Unknown variable 'formats'`, and `console.ask("n")` fails with `ParserError: Expected property name` because `ask` is a reserved keyword (that half is phase-049's work, not this phase's). `list.map([1,2,3], to (x) give back x*2 end)` DOES work and prints `[2, 4, 6]`, because `list` is in MODULES. The two names SPEC.md uses and MODULES omits are `text` (SPEC.md:952-957 documents uppercase, lowercase, split, join) and `math` (SPEC.md:960-966 documents PI, sqrt, random, round) — and `formats` (SPEC.md:995-800 documents parse_json, to_json, parse_csv), where `json` and `csv` are in MODULES and do work. SPEC.md:799 and SPEC.md:806-814 then build `catch error`/`might fail` examples on `formats.parse_json`, which is doubly unreachable. phase-032 owned this reconciliation and is `.blocked` — rbops/dispatch.sh:242 skips a `.blocked` id permanently and it has 0 commits on redblue main, so it will never run. phase-041 covers `text.split`/`text.join` specifically but explicitly defers the module-list reconciliation, so the name-level disagreement is still unowned.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Make `src/stdlib.rs`, SPEC.md and README.md name the same set of modules, so no module the specification documents is rejected as an unknown variable.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-050
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] a test reads SPEC.md and README.md, extracts the module names each documents, and fails when a documented name is absent from `MODULES` at src/stdlib.rs:7 or present in `MODULES` but documented nowhere — the extracted lists are pasted into REPORT.md
- [ ] every module name in SPEC.md's Standard Library section (SPEC.md:942-1000) is callable: a test runs one .rb file per documented name through `rb run` and asserts exit 0
- [ ] `text.uppercase("hi")` prints `HELLO` and `math.sqrt(9)` prints `3`, or SPEC.md is corrected to the names the code uses and the correction is named in REPORT.md — the decision is one or the other, not both
- [ ] the `formats` heading at SPEC.md:994 and the `json`/`csv` names that work are reconciled the same way, so SPEC.md:799 and :806-814 are built on calls that exist
- [ ] edge tests named edge_* cover: a documented module function called with no arguments, with too many, and with an argument of the wrong type — each a caught RuntimeError naming the function, never a panic — and an unknown module name (`nosuchmodule.read("x")`)
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets` reports 0 failures and every file in examples/ and modules/ still exits 0
